scoring.minor: 0.8-0.9: Minor issues (slightly short/long description, missing one OG tag)
scoring.moderate: 0.5-0.7: Moderate issues (no JSON-LD, missing canonical, poor description)
scoring.major: Below 0.5: Major issues (no meta description, no structured data, broken canonical)

metadata.context: The metadata provided was extracted from the initial server-side rendered (SSR) HTML response — i.e. the raw HTML returned before any client-side JavaScript runs. Mayo Clinic pages are Next.js applications; some meta tags (especially og:description and meta description) may be populated only after client-side hydration and will therefore appear missing or empty in the SSR snapshot. When reporting issues with missing or empty tags, note explicitly that the tag was absent in the SSR HTML and may be injected client-side, which means search engine crawlers that rely on the raw HTML response may also not see them.

rules.description: Meta description tag must be present in the SSR HTML
Meta description must be within 150-160 characters for optimal search engine display
Canonical URL must be present to prevent duplicate content issues
Canonical URL must match the submitted page URL
JSON-LD structured data must be present in the page
JSON-LD must contain at least one MedicalWebPage or WebPage schema type
Open Graph og:title tag must be present
Open Graph og:description tag must be present
Open Graph og:type must be set to 'website' or 'article'

scoring.perfect: 1.0: Excellent structure, up-to-date, proper attribution, complete sections
scoring.minor: 0.8-0.9: Minor issues (one missing section, slightly outdated review date)
scoring.moderate: 0.5-0.7: Moderate issues (poor heading structure, no review date, missing attribution)
scoring.major: Below 0.5: Major issues (no discernible structure, severely outdated, missing critical sections)

rules.description: H1 heading must be present and descriptive of the page topic
H2 headings must be used for major content sections (Symptoms, Causes, Treatment, etc.)
No heading level skips allowed (e.g., H4 must not appear without a preceding H3)
A 'last reviewed' date must be present on the page
Last reviewed date must be within 2 years (no earlier than 2024 for current year 2026)
Author attribution must be present — 'By Mayo Clinic Staff' or a named reviewer
At least 3 required sections must be present from: Overview, Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention
Body text should contain at least 500 words for adequate content depth
URL path and headings should suggest correct medical category (e.g., diseases-conditions, symptoms)

scoring.perfect: 1.0: Fully compliant, proper hedging, no prohibited language
scoring.minor: 0.8-0.9: Minor issues (one unsubstantiated claim, missing one disclaimer)
scoring.moderate: 0.5-0.7: Moderate issues (multiple policy violations, missing critical disclaimers)
scoring.major: Below 0.5: Major violations (absolute cure claims, HIPAA concerns, significant legal risk)

rules.description: Content must NOT contain absolute cure claims: 'cures', 'eliminates', 'eradicates', 'guarantees recovery/remission'
Content must NOT contain unsubstantiated superlatives: 'the only treatment', 'best medicine', 'revolutionary'
Content must NOT promote off-label drug use without appropriate FDA caveats
Content must NOT expose personal health information or patient-identifiable data
Required medical disclaimer language must be present (e.g., 'consult your healthcare provider')
Medical content should use appropriate hedging: 'may help', 'can reduce', 'consult a doctor' rather than absolute statements
Drug and treatment references must comply with FDA language guidelines — no unapproved claims

scoring.perfect: 1.0: All verifiable claims align with reference material
scoring.moderate: 0.5-0.7: Moderate inaccuracies (wrong dosage ranges, incorrect symptom attribution)
scoring.major: Below 0.5: Significant factual errors or contradictions with reference material

rules.description: All verifiable medical claims must align with retrieved reference material from the knowledge base
Drug dosage ranges and medication information must be accurate per reference material
Symptoms must be attributed to the correct conditions — no cross-condition symptom confusion
Statistics and numerical data should be current and match reference material
Medical terminology must be used precisely and consistently with reference material
If no relevant references are found in the knowledge base, score 0.7 and note the limitation

scoring.perfect: 1.0: No self-closing or empty content tags found

rules.description: Content tags must NOT be self-closing (e.g., <title/>, <h1 />) — they should contain content

Content tags must NOT be empty or whitespace-only (e.g., ,

)
The following tags are checked: title, h1, h2, h3, h4, p, a, li, td, th, label, button
